name: CEREBRON Benchmark V2.1 Leak-Resistant Weight Ablation
purpose: Test whether CEREBRON cognitive meta-weights change deterministic model-selection performance when final targets, latent parameters and domain labels are inaccessible to candidate logic.

hypotheses.H1: A0 weighted orchestration has lower held-out MAE than a neutral equal-resource selector.
hypotheses.H2: Representation transfer learned only from source tasks improves held-out target MAE over no-transfer A0.
hypotheses.H3: At least one used meta-weight has a measurable ablation effect on held-out performance.
hypotheses.H4: Any A1 candidate is rejected unless it improves held-out performance at equal resource while passing leakage and regression gates.

leakage_prohibitions: candidate logic cannot access final query target
candidate logic cannot access latent generator parameters
candidate logic cannot access generator family/domain label
verification uses only observable support split
failure signals use only observable validation residuals
transfer prior is learned only from source tasks

requirements: heldout MAE strictly lower than A0 on aggregate
positive result on at least 4 of 5 seeds
no heldout family regresses by more than 10 percent

claim_limit: This is a synthetic deterministic benchmark of orchestration meta-parameters. Success cannot establish AGI, superintelligence, neural-weight improvement, or external generalization.
